source_refs.note: Flower Colour in Foxglove: a main subheading of 18.5.2 Epistasis, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 99-100.

blocks.text: In foxglove plants, the flower colour (dark red, light red, and white) is controlled by interaction in two genes (gene D and gene W).

items: Gene D has a dominant allele D that produces dark red petals. Its recessive allele d produces light red petals. Therefore, a genotype DD or Dd will have dark red and a genotype dd will have light red flower colour.

Gene W (present at another locus) has a dominant allele W that limits the distribution of pigment (produced by D and d) in the form of small spots so petals appear white from outside. The recessive w allows uniform pigment distribution.

blocks.alt: In a dotted frame. Top: pictures of dark red, light red and white foxglove flower spikes with their genotypes: dark red DDww or Ddww; light red ddww; white DDWW, DDWw, DdWW, DdWw, ddWW or ddWw. Below: two white DdWw plants (white flowers shown) are crossed; a 4 x 4 grid with male gametes DW, Dw, dW, dw across and female gametes down gives each offspring's genotype and flower colour: twelve white, three dark red, one light red.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.9: Genotypes and phenotypes of flower colour in foxglove (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.9).
blocks.long_description: Grid rows (female gametes) DW, Dw, dW, dw. Row DW: DDWW, DDWw, DdWW, DdWw, all White. Row Dw: DDWw White, DDww Dark red, DdWw White, Ddww Dark red. Row dW: DdWW, DdWw, ddWW, ddWw, all White. Row dw: DdWw White, Ddww Dark red, ddWw White, ddww Light red.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed legend of Figure 18.9 reads 'DDWW or DdWW or DdWW or DdWw': DdWW is printed twice, and DDWw, ddWW and ddWw are missing. Every plant with at least one W allele is white, so there are six white genotypes (DDWW, DDWw, DdWW, DdWw, ddWW, ddWw), as drawn above.

The heterozygous plant DdWw will have white flowers (because the W allele limits the pigment in small spots in the inner side). If such heterozygous plant is self-fertilized, it produces plants with white, dark red and light red flowers in 12:3:1 ratio.
